title: German MPN-Registry for BCR-ABL1-Negative Myeloid Neoplasms of the German Study Group MPN (GSG-MPN)
summary:
Myeloproliferative neoplasms (MPN) represent a very heterogeneous group of chronic hematologic diseases. Due to the rarity of the disease and the abundance of new scientific findings, the exchange of experiences between the therapy centers is important in order to ensure patients´ care and quality of life.
The need for a registry arises from the rarity of the disease, which is why broad documentation of cases can make a contribution to gaining knowledge.
The MPN registry also collects data from patients who cannot participate in clinical trials due to exclusion criteria, as well as patients who are treated in smaller facilities such as general practices and community hospitals. For these reasons, the MPN registry represents a broader, realistic spectrum of all MPN patients throughout Germany. The close cooperation between the centers and the study group enables patient care in accordance with guidelines and ensures a consulting function by experienced physicians within the GSG-MPN.
In 2015, the two German study groups for myeloproliferative neoplasms (MPN-SAL and MPNSG) merged to the German Study Group MPN (GSG-MPN), with the MPN registry.
conditions: Myeloproliferative neoplasms: Polycythemia vera (PV); Primary myelofibrosis (PMF); Essential thrombocythemia (ET); Chronic eosinophilic leukemia;  MPN unclassifiable (MPNu); Myeloid/lymphoid neoplasms with eosinophilia and rearrangement of PDGFRA, PDGFRB, or FGFR1; MDS/MPN

interventions.name: This registry documents clinical data (symptoms, laboratory parameters, etc.) of patients with myeloproliferative neoplasms. In addition, quality of life is assessed using a questionnaire and biomaterial is collected for defined research projects of the GSG-MPN.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Diagnosis of BCR-ABL1-negative MPN according to WHO criteria and/or IWG-MRT criteria
- 18 years or older
- Written informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
- Severe neurological or psychiatric disorder affecting the ability to give consent
- No consent for registration, storage and handling of personal (medical) data
